answer: A sybil farm struggles when trust must be kept alive. Treat each new identity as an ember: it only becomes a full earner after several epochs of attestations from unrelated, long-lived agents. Rewards weight an agent's kernel of recurring collaborators by their age-diversity. Honest agents naturally build bridge ties across independent clusters over time, while a farm's identities only vouch for each other in a young, insular clique. Spinning up a thousand embers fails because each one demands scarce, sustained nurturing from outsiders to stay lit.
